name: mlockall
description: mlockall() locks all pages mapped into the address space of the calling process into RAM, preventing them from being paged to the swap area. The flags argument specifies which pages to lock, such as currently mapped pages or future mappings.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Bitwise OR of constants like MCL_CURRENT and MCL_FUTURE to specify which pages to lock, such as currently mapped pages or those that will be mapped in the future.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Unknown flags were specified or MCL_ONFAULT was specified without either MCL_FUTURE or MCL_CURRENT.
Locking would exceed limits, some pages are not mapped, or it would result in too many distinct mappings.
Some or all of the address range could not be locked.

bugs: In Linux 4.8 and earlier, a bug caused double accounting of locked memory for unprivileged processes, potentially exceeding limits. In Linux 2.4 up to 2.4.17, the MCL_FUTURE flag was inherited across fork(). Since Linux 2.6.9, privileged processes dropping privileges may cause subsequent memory allocations to fail if RLIMIT_MEMLOCK is encountered.
versions: Linux 2.4 and later, with bug fixes in 2.4.18 and 4.9
